links.outcome: Calibration of POSSUM/P-POSSUM before and after local logistic recalibration
links.effect: Original models underestimated events; bootstrap-corrected recalibration gave slopes 0.837-0.907 and intercepts 0.16 to -0.34, improving calibration without materially changing AUC.
links.quote: Our findings support the notion that logistic recalibration can reduce systematic calibration errors without materially changing discrimination [ 13 , 25 ].

links.outcome: Performance of POSSUM/P-POSSUM on local historical data against observed outcomes
links.effect: Local validation showed fair discrimination (AUC 0.696-0.755) and miscalibration, with observed event rates higher than median predicted risks, supporting local model updating.
links.quote: These observed rates were higher than the median predicted risks for both endpoints, indicating that the models tended to underestimate the event probability in this population.

links.outcome: Model discrimination and calibration by extent of resection subgroup (major vs minor hepatectomy)
links.effect: Major hepatectomy AUC 0.633 (slope 0.437) vs minor AUC 0.770 (slope 0.846); calibration differed between subgroups.
links.quote: Calibration differed between subgroups, with calibration slopes of 0.437(major) and 0.846 (minor) and calibration intercepts of − 0.067 (major) and − 0.456 (minor).

links.outcome: Performance of established generic risk models applied to a new specialized surgical population
links.effect: POSSUM/P-POSSUM showed fair discrimination and slopes below 1 in hepatic resection, needing recalibration.
links.quote: OOB bootstrap calibration showed slopes below 1 for all endpoints (clinically relevant morbidity: α 0.16, β 0.837, Brier 0.172; major morbidity: α − 0.051, β 0.907, Brier 0.215; mortality: α − 0.34, β 0.843, Brier 0.068), supporting the need for local model updating.

links.outcome: Net benefit of recalibrated models versus treat-all and operative severity proxy in decision curve analysis
links.effect: For any morbidity, no incremental benefit over treat-all or proxy; major morbidity exceeded treat-all in 76.3% of thresholds and proxy in 46.1%; mortality exceeded proxy in 85.2%.
links.quote: Compared with the operative severity proxy (mean net benefit 0.173), the recalibrated model was higher in 46.1% of the thresholds, suggesting a modest and threshold-dependent incremental advantage (Fig. 4 B).

links.outcome: local morbidity and mortality prediction performance
links.effect: AUCs: 0.696 clinically relevant morbidity, 0.697 major morbidity, 0.755 mortality; calibration slopes below 1 supported local updating.
links.quote: OOB bootstrap calibration showed slopes below 1 for all endpoints (clinically relevant morbidity: α 0.16, β 0.837, Brier 0.172; major morbidity: α − 0.051, β 0.907, Brier 0.215; mortality: α − 0.34, β 0.843, Brier 0.068), supporting the need for local model updating.

links.outcome: local logistic recalibration of risk models
links.effect: After recalibration/OOB: ≥II α 0.16, β 0.837, Brier 0.172; ≥IIIa α −0.051, β 0.907, Brier 0.215; mortality α −0.34, β 0.843, Brier 0.068.
links.quote: In this single-center cohort of 194 elective hepatic resections, POSSUM showed fair discrimination and imperfect calibration for morbidity outcomes, which improved after bootstrap-corrected logistic recalibration, supporting its use for institutional benchmarking and preoperative risk communication when locally validated and updated.

links.effect: Major hepatectomy AUC 0.633 versus minor hepatectomy AUC 0.770; calibration slopes 0.437 versus 0.846.
links.quote: For the prediction of major morbidity (Clavien–Dindo ≥ IIIa) using the POSSUM predicted morbidity risk, discrimination was AUC 0.633 (95% CI 0.535–0.733) in major hepatectomy ( n = 126, events = 56) and AUC 0.770 (95% CI 0.638–0.885) in minor hepatectomy ( n = 68, events = 17).

links.effect: Any morbidity: mean NB 0.645 identical to treat-all; major: exceeded treat-all 76.3%, proxy 46.1%; mortality: exceeded treat-all 97.7%, proxy 85.2%.
links.quote: Overall, the decision curves suggest the greatest incremental clinical utility of recalibrated predictions for major morbidity and in-hospital mortality, while for any morbidity, the net benefit was comparable to treat-all and the operative severity proxy within the examined threshold range.

links.outcome: calibration of morbidity and mortality predictions
links.effect: Calibration slopes were 0.837 for clinically relevant morbidity, 0.907 for major morbidity, and 0.843 for mortality (Brier scores 0.172, 0.215, 0.068), improving model fit after bootstrap-corrected logistic recalibration.
links.quote: In this single-center cohort of 194 elective hepatic resections, POSSUM showed fair discrimination and imperfect calibration for morbidity outcomes, which improved after bootstrap-corrected logistic recalibration, supporting its use for institutional benchmarking and preoperative risk communication when locally validated and updated.

screen.reason: The study directly evaluates the deployment practice of local validation and logistic recalibration of existing risk prediction models (POSSUM and P-POSSUM) before clinical implementation.
